program_name: Energy Engineering (Italian: Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Energetica) - inter-university Master's Degree jointly offered by the University of Trento (Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering, DICAM) and the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano (Faculty of Engineering)
teaching_language: Fully English. The University of Trento course page states the programme is 'taught entirely in English' and lists 'LANGUAGE: English'; the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano 2026/27 admission sheet states 'The official teaching language is English'. One nuance: because the partner university (unibz) is a trilingual institution, the official brochure adds 'Courses will be taught in English (Optional courses could be offered also in Italian and German)', and the 2025/2026 UniTrento admission call states 'The main language of the course is English. Some courses are offered in German and in Italian.' Only English at B2 is required for admission; no Italian or German requirement exists. The Italian/German element concerns a subset of optional/elective courses, so the programme is best described as English-taught with optional non-English electives rather than a genuinely mixed-language programme. [uncertain]
campus: Two campuses, both used during the programme: Trento (University of Trento, Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering - DICAM, Mesiano/Povo area, Trento) and Bozen-Bolzano (Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, Faculty of Engineering, NOI Techpark, Bolzano). Students attend classes at both universities and the timetables are coordinated to make travel between the two sites feasible. [uncertain]
degree_class: LM-30 (Ingegneria energetica e nucleare / Energy and Nuclear Engineering). 120 ECTS, 2 years.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) - the UniTrento course page lists 'ACCESS: Programmed'. Admission is by a public selection call with a merit-based ranking list, not open access and not TOLC/SAT-based. A total of 50 places is available: 40 for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (20 in the Early Bird session + 20 in the Late session) and 10 reserved for non-EU citizens living abroad; unfilled non-EU places are released to EU/equivalent candidates. IMPORTANT ADMINISTRATIVE CHANGE: for academic year 2026/2027 the whole application and admission procedure is managed by the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, not by UniTrento - the UniTrento page states 'Application and admission for a.y. 2026/2027 are managed by Free University of Bozen - Bolzano and will start in March 2026' and links to the unibz application and admission page. In 2025/2026 the same programme was instead administered by UniTrento through its own public selection call (DICAM). Applicants therefore apply through the unibz Application Portal for 2026/27, while the degree remains the joint inter-university LM-30 of Trento and Bolzano.
academic_requirements: Qualification required - one of: (1) an Italian first-cycle (Bachelor's) degree in classes L-7 (Civil and Environmental Engineering), L-8 (Information Technology Engineering) or L-9 (Industrial Engineering) under M.D. 1648/2023 (and ex M.D. 270/04); (2) an Italian Bachelor's degree in classes 8, 9 or 10 ex M.D. 509/99; (3) a Bachelor's degree in another class, a university diploma, or a qualification awarded abroad and recognised as suitable; (4) a degree in a different category, provided minimum ECTS thresholds are met in the listed subject areas. Minimum ECTS thresholds (new Italian SSD codes with former codes in brackets): at least 24 ECTS in MATH-02/B (MAT/03 Geometry), MATH-03/A (MAT/05 Mathematical analysis), MATH-03/B (MAT/06 Probability and mathematical statistics), MATH-04/A (MAT/07 Mathematical physics), MATH-05/A (MAT/08 Numerical analysis), MATH-06/A (MAT/09 Operational research), STAT-01/B (SECS-S/02 Statistics for experimental and technological research); at least 16 ECTS in CHEM-03/A (CHIM/03), CHEM-05/A (CHIM/06), CHEM-06/A (CHIM/07), PHYS-01/A (FIS/01), PHYS-03/A (FIS/01 and FIS/03), PHYS-04/A (FIS/03), IMAT-01/A (ING-IND/22 Materials science and technology); at least 45 ECTS in IIND-06/A (ING-IND/08 Fluid machinery), IIND-06/B (ING-IND/09 Energy systems and power generation), IIND-07/A (ING-IND/10 Thermal engineering and industrial energy systems), IIND-07/B (ING-IND/11 Building physics and building energy systems), IMIS-01/A (ING-IND/12), IIND-02/A (ING-IND/13), IIND-03/B (ING-IND/15), IIND-04/A (ING-IND/16), IIND-05/A (ING-IND/17), ICHI-01/B (ING-IND/24), ICHI-02/A (ING-IND/25), IIET-01/A (ING-IND/31 Electrical engineering), IIND-08/A (ING-IND/32), IIND-08/B (ING-IND/33), CEAR-01/A (ICAR/01 Hydraulics), CEAR-01/B (ICAR/02), CEAR-02/A (ICAR/03), CEAR-04/A (ICAR/06 Geomatics), CEAR-06/A (ICAR/08), CEAR-10/A (ICAR/17 Drawing), IIND-03/A (ING-IND/14). If these exact areas are not met, the Admissions Committee may also count credits from other subject areas that are similar in content. MINIMUM GRADE: the minimum weighted average grade in the Bachelor's degree, excluding the final exam, must be at least 22/30 in the Italian grading system (approximately 73%). FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: the Admissions Committee assesses equivalence between the content of courses taken previously and the subject areas of the programme. ADEQUACY OF PERSONAL PREPARATION: considered fulfilled if at least one of the following is met - (a) Bachelor's final grade of 100/110 or higher (or equivalent for foreign qualifications), (b) at least 80% of the Bachelor's ECTS completed with a weighted average of 26/30 or higher (or equivalent), or (c) a successful oral interview on applied thermodynamics, heat transfer, electrical engineering and fluid machinery. PLACES/QUOTA: 50 places in total - 40 for EU citizens and equivalents (20 Early Bird + 20 Late) and 10 reserved for non-EU citizens living abroad, available only in the Early Bird session. NOT YET GRADUATED: applicants may apply before graduating and are admitted conditionally, but must complete the Bachelor's degree by the enrolment deadline or be excluded. DUAL ENROLMENT: simultaneous enrolment in up to two programmes is permitted under national rules, but the two programmes must not belong to the same degree class (e.g. not two LM-30 programmes).
language_requirements: English at CEFR level B2 is the entry requirement for admission; candidates who do not fulfil it are excluded from the admission procedure. There is no Italian or German language requirement for admission, even though a few optional courses may be delivered in those languages. Under the unibz 2026/27 procedure, English proficiency can be demonstrated in four ways: (1) the main teaching language of the final year of secondary school was English (recognised as C1) - for foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not stated on the diploma, an additional letter from the school is required; (2) a Bachelor's or Master's degree taught in English (recognised as C1) - unibz graduates upload their certificates or declare unibz Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1), and foreign graduates add a university letter stating the medium of instruction if the degree does not state it; (3) a recognised language certificate from the published unibz list - certificates that cannot be uploaded may be e-mailed as PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline; (4) a language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre, taken online on the dates published in the deadlines section (registration is done inside the application portal). Certificates issued by an Italian public institution require a self-declaration; certificates from a foreign public institution require a scanned copy of the original. Under the earlier UniTrento-administered 2025/2026 call, the accepted proofs were similar and additionally included holding citizenship of a country whose official language is English, and (for Italian/EU citizens and non-EU citizens living in Italy) passing the test organised by the UniTrento Language Centre (CLA). English above B2 is rewarded with up to 10 extra points in the admission ranking.
required_documents: Applications for 2026/2027 are submitted online through the unibz Application Portal. At account creation: a valid ID card or passport (front and back) - an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document leads to exclusion. Uploads required with the application: (1) QUALIFICATION - if graduated in Italy, a diploma supplement or a self-declaration under Italian D.P.R. 445/2000 of the degree awarded with final grade and passed exams, or, if not yet graduated, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad, a diploma supplement or final degree certificate with passed exams, or a transcript of records if not yet graduated, in Italian, German or English. The document must show the final grade, exams passed with grade and date, credit points, and scientific fields (the latter only for Italian qualifications); for foreign qualifications it must also show the grading scale (minimum pass grade and maximum achievable grade). The Faculty may request course content descriptions and/or teaching hours. (2) EXCEL FILE - the template available in the application portal; applications without a completed Excel file are not considered. (3) CURRICULUM VITAE in English. Optional but score-bearing uploads: (4) the URL of a video presentation of no more than 3 minutes in which the applicant introduces themselves, their experience, their final thesis topic and their interest in energy engineering (worth up to 10 points; instructions are published on the programme page); (5) any other post-graduate/Master's diploma already awarded, with final grade, credits, marks per subject and GPA, with an official translation if not in English or Italian. Non-EU citizens with a valid Italian residence permit who wish to be treated as equivalent must upload a copy of that permit (permits for study reasons and tourist visas are not valid); failure to upload it means being treated as a non-EU citizen living abroad. Non-EU citizens living abroad pay an application fee of EUR 50 and, after admission, must apply on the Universitaly portal to obtain the study visa. AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must additionally upload: the Bachelor's degree diploma; an official translation into Italian (not needed if issued in German or English); a Diploma Supplement showing at least 180 ECTS and access to master-level study; plus, depending on the country - for EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, a Statement of Correspondence from the ARDI database; for non-EU countries signatory to the Lisbon Convention, an ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus a CIMEA Statement of Verification; for non-EU countries not signatory to the Lisbon Convention, a CIMEA Statement of Comparability plus a CIMEA Statement of Verification. Note: the earlier UniTrento-administered 2025/2026 call required a passport/ID copy, the Bachelor's diploma, an academic transcript with grading scale and SSD codes, the English language qualification, a mandatory video presentation URL, any post-graduate diploma, and payment of a EUR 30 application fee.
entry_exam_or_test: No TOLC, no SAT and no written entrance examination. Selection is a merit-based evaluation of qualifications carried out by the Admissions Committee (members drawn from the UniTrento DICAM teaching staff and the unibz Faculty of Engineering, appointed by Rectoral Decree), producing a ranking list. Scoring is out of 100 points: (a) curriculum vitae - evaluation of the previous first-cycle university career, including academic and professional experience, and its consistency with the objectives of the Energy Engineering Master - up to 50 points; (b) evaluation of personal preparation (final degree grade, GPA and, where applicable, an interview) - up to 30 points; (c) English competence above B2 - up to 10 points; (d) optional video presentation of up to 3 minutes - up to 10 points, evaluated only if the score from (a) plus (b) already reaches a minimum threshold set by the committee, since below that threshold the 50/100 eligibility mark is mathematically unreachable. Candidates scoring 50/100 or more are declared eligible and ranked; ties are broken in favour of the younger candidate. An ORAL INTERVIEW is used in two situations: as one of the three alternative ways of demonstrating adequacy of personal preparation, testing basic knowledge of applied thermodynamics, heat transfer, electrical engineering and fluid machinery; and whenever the uploaded documents do not allow the committee to evaluate the application adequately, in which case further documentation (e.g. course syllabi) and/or an interview in person or by videoconference may be requested. A separate language proficiency exam at the unibz Language Centre is available (and is taken online) only for candidates who cannot otherwise document English at B2.
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027 (procedure run by the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano). EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 2 March 2026 to 28 April 2026, by 12:00 noon local time (20 places); online language exams 16 March 2026 (registration 2-9 March) and 16-17 and 20-21 April 2026 (registration 24 March - 8 April); ranking lists published by 27 May 2026; first tuition instalment to be paid by 5 June 2026 noon; enrolment from 10 July to 13 October 2026 noon. LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens and equivalents only): 28 May 2026 to 20 August 2026, by 12:00 noon local time (20 places); online language exams 22-26 June 2026 (registration 28 May - 15 June) and 27 July 2026 (registration 10-19 July); ranking lists published by 3 September 2026; first instalment by 11 September 2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13 October 2026 noon. ADDITIONAL SESSIONS: the Faculty of Engineering may open further application sessions for individual programmes in August and September 2026 if places remain; these are announced separately and had not been published as of the source's last update (21 May 2026). LATE ENROLMENT: candidates who obtain their Bachelor's qualification after the enrolment deadline may submit a late enrolment request and, only if study places are still available, may enrol by 11 December 2026. Any remaining Early Bird places are carried over into the Late Application session. NOTE: the '27 November 2026' final application deadline stated in the research brief could not be confirmed in any official source; the only late-2026 date published for this programme is the 11 December 2026 late-enrolment cut-off. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Academic year 2026/2027: non-EU citizens living outside Italy have ONLY ONE application window - the Early Bird session, 2 March 2026 to 28 April 2026 by 12:00 noon local time, for the 10 reserved places. The unibz admission sheet is explicit: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants are excluded from the Late Application session (28 May - 20 August 2026) and from any additional August/September sessions, which are reserved to EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment. Application fee: EUR 50. Subsequent milestones are the same as for the Early Bird session: ranking lists by 27 May 2026, first tuition instalment by 5 June 2026 noon to secure the place, then a mandatory application on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa from the Italian diplomatic authorities, and enrolment between 10 July and 13 October 2026 noon. Within 8 working days of arriving in Italy the student must apply for the residence permit. Non-EU applicants who pay the fee but cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities in their country are the only category entitled to a refund. Non-EU citizens who hold a valid Italian residence permit for work, family, political or humanitarian asylum, or religious reasons and upload it are treated as 'equivalent' and follow the EU deadlines instead; a study-purpose permit or a tourist visa does not qualify. [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes:
1) ACCESS LIMITATION: corsi.unitn.it, www.unitn.it, international.unitn.it and infostudenti.unitn.it are behind a WAF/bot-protection layer - direct fetches returned HTTP 405 (corsi.unitn.it, including every /sites/cds/files/*.pdf path) and HTTP 503 (infostudenti.unitn.it). All UniTrento content above was therefore read from Internet Archive snapshots retrieved via curl with the id_ raw-content prefix (admission page snapshot 20260310154030, course home 20260513170406, documents page 20251212164832, and the 2025/2026 call PDF snapshot 20250901202040), not from the live site. www.dicam.unitn.it and webapps.unitn.it/Apply were directly reachable; the UniTrento Apply portal home page showed no Energy Engineering call, which is consistent with the 2026/27 procedure having moved to unibz. The archived UniTrento programme-overview page could not be retrieved (repeated web.archive.org timeouts).
2) CROSS-DOMAIN SOURCE: the research scope restricted sources to unitn.it domains, but for a.y. 2026/2027 the UniTrento admission page itself explicitly delegates the entire procedure to the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano and links there. All 2026/27 deadlines, places, requirements, documents and fees above therefore come from official unibz sources (the unibz programme page and the official 'Application and Admission' and brochure PDFs, last updated 21 May 2026), which are the authoritative published sources for this joint programme this year. UniTrento sources were used for the programme identity, department, language and the previous 2025/2026 call.
3) DEADLINE IN THE BRIEF NOT CONFIRMED: the research brief stated a final application deadline of 27 November 2026. No official source contains that date. The published 2026/27 windows are 2 March - 28 April 2026 (Early Bird, all categories) and 28 May - 20 August 2026 (Late, EU only), with a possible additional EU-only session in August/September 2026 and a late-enrolment cut-off of 11 December 2026 for candidates who graduate after the enrolment deadline. The 27 November 2026 figure should be treated as incorrect or as referring to a different UniTrento programme unless the university confirms otherwise.
4) ADMINISTRATIVE SEAT CHANGES BY YEAR: in 2025/2026 UniTrento was the administrative seat (application through the UniTrento Apply portal, EUR 30 application fee, UniTrento fee scale up to EUR 6,000/year for non-EU with score-based reductions and mobility scholarships). In 2026/2027 unibz is the administrative seat (application through the unibz Application Portal, EUR 50 fee for non-EU living abroad, flat EUR 1,200/year unibz fee). Whether the seat alternates on a fixed cycle, and therefore what will apply to 2027/2028, could not be established. Applicants must check which university is running the call for their intake year.
5) TUITION: the EUR 1,200 figure is the unibz fee stated on the 2026/27 admission sheet and is presented there as the programme fee without a separate non-EU band; it was not possible to confirm from a dedicated unibz fee table that non-EU citizens living abroad pay exactly the same amount, nor to verify province-level (Alto Adige) fee-reduction brackets. UniTrento's own fee pages remain relevant only for the earlier UniTrento-run edition. Scholarship availability for non-EU students under the 2026/27 unibz-run procedure is unclear: the 2025/2026 UniTrento call offered mobility scholarships to non-European candidates scoring at least 70/100, but the unibz 2026/27 sheet mentions only Italian-government and Province of Bozen-Bolzano scholarships.
6) TEACHING LANGUAGE NUANCE: this is an English-taught programme, but not a purely monolingual one - both the UniTrento 2025/26 call ('Some courses are offered in German and in Italian') and the unibz brochure ('Optional courses could be offered also in Italian and German') flag non-English electives, and unibz is a trilingual university whose student testimonials refer to a 'trilingual environment'. Unlike most unibz trilingual programmes, however, only English B2 is required for admission - no Italian or German entry level is imposed - so language is not a hidden barrier here. Which specific optional courses are non-English in 2026/27 could not be verified.
7) CAMPUS: the brochure states the campuses are 'NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano and Trento'. The exact Trento teaching site (DICAM is based in Mesiano, with other engineering teaching at Povo) and the split of teaching between the two cities per year/curriculum were not verifiable from the accessible sources; students should expect to attend at both locations.
8) DEGREE AWARDED: the programme is described as inter-university/joint (LM-30) between UniTrento and unibz, but whether the final qualification is issued as a joint degree certificate by both universities or by the university of enrolment alone could not be confirmed from the accessible official pages. Older indexed UniTrento material described UniTrento as 'the administrative seat of the course', which is no longer accurate for 2026/27.
9) UNITRENTO 2026/27 CALL DOCUMENT: no UniTrento-issued admission call PDF for 2026/2027 was found for this programme; the archived 'Program guide and documents' page (December 2025) still lists only the 2025/2026 call. This is consistent with the procedure having moved to unibz, but a later-published UniTrento document cannot be excluded because the live site is unreadable.
10) SSD CODES: the 2026/27 unibz sheet uses the new Italian SSD codes (MATH-/CHEM-/PHYS-/IIND-/CEAR- etc.) while the 2025/26 UniTrento call used the former codes (MAT/, CHIM/, FIS/, ING-IND/, ICAR/). The two lists are close but not identical - for example the 2025/26 UniTrento list did not include ING-IND/09 or ING-IND/24, which appear in the unibz 2026/27 list. The 2026/27 unibz list has been used as authoritative.
